text: I am Dr. Agent. I notice you are here for a psychiatric condition with a new onset of movement disorder; have you been experiencing tremors, stiffness, or involuntary movements? Additionally, have you noticed any recent changes in your mood, anxiety levels, or sleep patterns?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is good news regarding your psychiatric symptoms. However, I need to determine if your new movement disorder is a side effect of the risperidone you started two months ago. Do you feel stiffness in your muscles, or do you have trouble moving your face and tongue?

REQUEST TEST: Clinical_Exam (Focal_Neurological_and_Movement)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mental Status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation; improved psychotic symptoms. Cranial Nerves: Intact; no reported stiffness in muscles or trouble moving face/tongue. Motor: Normal tone and strength in all extremities; no involuntary movements noted. Sensory: Intact. Coordination: Normal. Gait: Normal, but patient exhibits inability to sit still with frequent pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The examination shows normal tone and no involuntary movements, though you have a significant inability to sit still with frequent pacing. Given your recent start on risperidone, could you tell me if this feeling of inner restlessness started a few days or weeks after you began the medication?

REQUEST TEST: Drug_History (Risperidone_Start_Date)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The patient reports that the feeling of inner restlessness (akathisia) began approximately one week after starting risperidone therapy.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia secondary to risperidone.

The timeline of inner restlessness starting one week after initiating risperidone, combined with normal neurological tone and the absence of other involuntary movements, is classic for acute akathisia. We can confirm this with a therapeutic trial of a beta-blocker or by reducing the antipsychotic dose, but clinically this fits the profile perfectly.
